column1: # core/lang/languages.tsv - the language registry (L1; contract in
# core/include/doomo/lang.h). tools/langpack.py builds core/gen/lang_ids.h
# (the LANG_* enum) and core/gen/lang_registry.c (doomo_lang_info[], the
# names the Options row shows, the table of each language) from it.
# Columns (TAB separated, UTF-8):
#   code    BCP 47 tag; the UI strings live in core/lang/<code>/ui_*.tsv
#           (English is the source text: it has no directory). The C name
#           is the code in lower case with '-' -> '_' (pt-BR: LANG_PT_BR,
#           core/gen/lang_tab_pt_br.c, doomo_lang_pt_br).
#   save    the byte saved in the island's options (OPT_LANGUAGE) and the
#           enum value. APPEND-ONLY: rows stay in save order, a new
#           language takes the next byte, a byte is never reused or
#           reordered (a save made with it would load as another
#           language). Retire a language by setting ready to 0, never by
#           deleting its row. At most LANG_SLOTS (10) languages: the file
#           directories that hold one entry per language (TEXT.BIN,
#           LANG.BIN) reserve 10 slots, so adding one never moves them.
#   name    the language's name in itself, as the Options row and the
#           title screen show it (never translated). Letters the font
#           does not have yet are drawn without their accent until the
#           glyph pages (L4) add them; a ready language's name must be
#           drawable as it is.
#   glyphs  how the text is encoded: latin = one byte per glyph, ASCII
#           plus the letters at 0xA0..0xFF of its glyph page. cjk2 is
#           reserved for Japanese and Chinese and NOT implemented yet
#           (lang.h "LATER: CJK"); langpack refuses it.
#   page    the glyph page that fills 0xA0..0xFF for this language. 0 is
#           the page that exists today (the Spanish letters, font.h
#           STR_ES_*); L4 adds per-language pages.
#   plural  the plural rule (lang_plural()): one = 1 is singular (2 forms),
#           zero_one = 0 and 1 are singular (2 forms), pl = Polish (one /
#           few / many: 3 forms), none = no plural (1 form, CJK later).
#   ready   1 = offered on the Options row and the title screen; 0 = known
#           to the engine (saves, the runner's `lang CODE`, tables) but not
#           offered to players yet (its translation is not done).
# code
en
es
pt-BR
fr
de
it
nl
pl
# Reserved, later (do not reuse these bytes): ja 8 and zh 9, glyphs cjk2,
# plural none.
